text: Levan Makhashvili - Both the European Parliament's documents and the European Parliament itself have, unfortunately, lost their value - the only thing left is a sporting interest: to see whether they will develop a document worse than the previous one or if we will have something new (05.05.2026, 14:29)

"This document, along with its amendments which made the initial version even worse, is completely detached from reality. For us and for society, European Parliament documents and the European Parliament itself have unfortunately lost value, as they do not serve the agenda of cooperation and dialogue," stated Levan Makhashvili, Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee on European Integration, responding to the report on Georgia adopted by the European Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee.
According to him/her, today the European Parliament's agenda is not in line with the Georgia-EU agenda and, in general, with the agenda for a better, peaceful future for Georgia.

"What can I tell you? You already know what we would do with this resolution [I would hand it in as waste paper]—for a simple reason: this document, along with its amendments which made the initial version even worse, is completely detached from reality. It is especially clear during these days and weeks who is actually obstructing the dialogue. It is precisely the European Parliament, in the form of these specific political groups, who, driven by their narrow political agendas, are doing their utmost to hinder dialogue. If we look at the developments of previous years, this is exactly what used to happen: whenever there was a prospect of resetting relations, dialogue, or cooperation, the European Parliament would swim against the current, and we are witnessing the same today."

"Therefore, for us and for the public, both the European Parliament's documents and the European Parliament itself have unfortunately lost their value, as they do not serve the agenda of cooperation and dialogue. Today, the European Parliament's agenda does not align with the Georgia-EU agenda or, more generally, with the agenda for Georgia's better, peaceful future," stated Levan Makhashvili.

In response to a question regarding the European Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee calling for sanctions against several Georgian media outlets in its adopted report, Makhashvili replied that the statements and entries in this specific document are laughable.

For information, the European Parliament's Committee on Foreign Affairs has adopted a report on Georgia. In the European Parliament's Committee on Foreign Affairs, 53 MEPs supported the annual report on Georgia, while 14 voted against it.
